# Tables and lists

> Settled 2026-09-09. Answers the list-feature matrix of `analysis/ui/TABLES_LISTS_SELECTION.md`
> (removed there once built; what that file still holds is below under "What this does not settle")
> and `analysis/ui/EMPTY_AND_LOADING_STATES.md`.

## 1. Which list gets what

The audit's finding was that features appear where somebody happened to build them. These are the
rules, and **the absences are as deliberate as the presences**.

| Feature | Where |
|---|---|
| **Sort** | **The People table and Documents only.** Nowhere else. |
| **Search** | **Everywhere.** Every list surface. |
| **Filter** | **Lists of people** — the People table, the company calendar board, the Attendance overview — and **query screens** (§ 1a). |
| **Show archived** | **Everywhere it applies** — every list whose records can be archived. |
| **Skeleton** | **Everywhere.** |
| **Empty state** | **Everywhere.** |
| **No search results** | **Everywhere.** |

**Sort is deliberately narrow.** A sortable column that nothing indicates is worse than no sorting —
the two screens that have it show the direction only after a click, so a sortable column is invisible
until used. Adding that to fourteen more screens multiplies the problem. People and Documents are the
two lists long enough for sorting to be the way somebody finds a row; everywhere else, search is.

**Filter is narrower still.** Filtering means the audience builder, which is a real piece of
machinery with `CUSTOM` access scopes behind it. It belongs where the population is genuinely large
and heterogeneous, which is people — **a list whose rows are people**, not only the People table. Amended
2026-09-28, when the owner asked for it on the Attendance overview; the calendar board had already
broken the narrower rule. The control is the shared `components/audience/FilterPopover` — the People
table and the board still draw it by hand, and move to it when next touched.

### 1a. Three kinds of list (decided 2026-10-27)

The owner settled what the table above left open — why the **Logs** page has filters and infinite scroll
when the rule said filters live with people. There are three kinds of list, and each kind decides its
features:

| Kind | Examples | Filters | Paging |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The People table** | People | The audience builder, saved views | Keyset pages |
| **A query screen** — read-only, its job is to answer a question about many records | Logs; a future usage report; the import history | **Column filters** — simple selects and a date range over one table, no builder, no scopes | **Infinite scroll** |
| **A list a person maintains** — tens of records somebody curates | Roles, offices, leave types, leave policies, holiday calendars | None — a search box at most | **None**: everything is loaded, until a list really grows past a few hundred |

A new screen picks its kind first; the kind answers the rest. A lists-of-people screen other than the
People table (the calendar board, the Attendance overview) keeps the shared `FilterPopover`.

## 2. Skeletons

**Every list has one, and it has the shape of the table it is standing in for.** The product had
thirteen hand-written skeletons and several screens with none; where one exists it often shows a
generic stack of bars that does not match the columns underneath it, so the layout jumps when the
data lands.

A skeleton is a promise about what is coming. Same column count, same widths, same row height.

**The form that cannot drift: skeleton rows inside the real `<TableBody>`**, under the real header, so
they inherit its columns and widths. A skeleton rendered *instead of* the table has to restate the
header and the widths, and the two that did got both wrong — five bars at invented widths for a
six-column table, with the header appearing from nowhere when the rows landed. **A centred spinner is
not a skeleton**: it is the same shape whatever is coming, which is the whole problem.

## 3. The three empty screens are three different screens

They mean different things and must not share a rendering. The product had six treatments plus a bare
line of grey text, and did not reliably distinguish these cases at all.

| Situation | What it says | What it offers |
|---|---|---|
| **Nothing exists yet** | An icon, a heading, one sentence | **The create action, and the whole block is clickable.** This is the screen somebody sees on their first day; it is the most valuable place in the product to put the primary action |
| **Search found nothing** | An icon, a heading, "Try a different …" | Nothing to create — the records exist, the query missed |
| **Could not load** | `ErrorState` | Retry — see `technical_documentation/ERRORS.md` |

**"Nothing here" and "we could not ask" are never the same screen.** That is the README's third rule,
and it is the one this document exists to enforce on lists.

Both the empty state and the no-results state are **designed screens**, not a sentence in grey.

**The components.** `EmptyState` and `NoResults` are two components, not one with a flag — they say
different things and only one may offer a create action. `EmptyState` renders as a `<button>` when it
carries that action, so the affordance is reachable by keyboard and announced.

A list does not choose between them itself: **`ListEmptyState` asks the question in one order** — did
the search miss, is this an empty archive, or does nothing exist yet — because writing that ladder at
every call site is how it drifts, and getting it wrong is silent: every branch renders something
plausible. **The create action is gated inside `ListEmptyState`** (`createAccess` puts it behind a
`PermissionGate`), so a reader who may not create sees the same panel without the affordance. **Not in
`EmptyState`**: a gate there makes a shared leaf component depend on react-query, and every test that
renders it then needs a `QueryClientProvider`.

**A list that is one section of a page** — *To Write* on My Reviews, a cycle's reviewers, the peers of a
nomination — gets `EmptyState` with `compact` (2026-11-03): the same icon, heading and sentence in less room,
so an empty section does not outweigh the full ones around it. Never a bare line of grey text.

## 4. Show archived

The toggle's behaviour, its position and the rule about hiding it when nothing is archived are in
[`ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md`](ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md) § 5, because it lives in the toolbar.

Worth repeating here: it is a **switch between two views**, not an "also include". Choosing this
means an archived list is a first-class screen and needs its own empty state ("Nothing archived"),
which is the case § 3 would otherwise miss.

## 5. Lists inside a card

From the designers' home round (`hris/design/handoffs/2026-11-11-home/PRODUCT-RULES.md`), taken by the owner on 2026-11-11.

- **A card never grows with its content**: its list scrolls inside, with a fade at the bottom and a thin thumb.
- **A count next to a title is a counter pill**, not a number in brackets.
- **A list of what waits shows only what waits**: a signed document, a done task, an answered request leave it (they
  stay on their own page). **A done task stays crossed out until the end of that day**, then leaves — so Undo has
  somewhere to happen.
- **Days and dates in a list of what is coming are in the accent** ("Thu 12").

## What this does not settle

- Paging inside a lists-of-people screen other than the People table. § 1a settles query screens and
  maintained lists; the calendar board pages people 25 at a time and the Attendance overview has its own.
- **Whether "every list surface" includes a short sub-list inside a screen that already searches** — the
  holiday-days editor, the balance ledger, the profile's time-off requests. None has search; a second box
  in the same panel may be worse than none.
- **Show archived on a canvas.** Departments and teams archive, but their screen is a canvas, not a list,
  and "switch the canvas to the archived view" is a different question from the toolbar toggle.
- Row click, in general. Some rows open a detail page, some do nothing, some have the action only in the
  kebab. Two lists open a detail page on a row click — Processes and the Attendance overview — the
  whole row, `cursor-pointer`, Enter from the keyboard; that is the shape to copy, but it is not yet a rule.
- Selection and bulk actions outside the People table.
- The sort indicator itself — a sortable-but-unsorted column has no affordance in either of the two
  screens that sort.
